title: Digging a well while the house burns
literal_meaning: Digging a well when the house is burning.
meaning_odia: ଘର ପୋଡ଼ିବା ବେଳେ ନିଆଁ ଲିଭାଇବାକୁ ପାଣି ଦରକାର, ଅଥଚ ସେତେବେଳେ କୂଅ ଖୋଳା ଆରମ୍ଭ ହେଉଛି। ଦରକାର ପଡ଼ିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ କରିବାକୁ ଥିବା ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତିକୁ ସଙ୍କଟ ଆସିବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ପକାଇରଖିବା ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଉପହାସର ବିଷୟ।
explanation: The emergency needs water now, but the work of making a water source is only beginning. Read editorially, the saying mocks preparation delayed until the crisis it should have anticipated. The inspected public gloss calls the situation laughable.
usage_example: Original imagined example: An event is about to begin when the organisers discover that they have never arranged the essential equipment. As they start searching for it, someone compares their timing to digging a well while the house burns.
cultural_context: The house fire and the unfinished well compress two different timescales into one scene: an urgent need and work that must precede it. The humour lies in treating the moment of need as the moment to begin preparing.
